title: Compute the constitution's cathedral kill condition from git and the ledger, and fail any machine-readable reality claim above what its evidence kind can establish
problem: Two gaps at the unit's base 44b3df96 (#236's head), still present at #196's head d35d92a5. (1) constitution/constitution.ucl declares kill_condition 'cathedral' ('activity rises while external outcomes remain unchanged, or the Kernel adds more cost than control'; then 'suspend_expansion_and_escalate(alfonso)'), and compiler/ucl_compiler.py parses it, but nothing evaluated it. Directive section 55 asks to 'Continuously test for' that shape and 'STOP HORIZONTAL EXPANSION'. `greg cathedral` exited 2 ('invalid choice'). (2) Directive section 56 says 'Do not collapse these' levels, and INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN names as failure 'a container run reported as founder-used'. Nothing read the repository's machine-readable claims against their evidence. Measured on a git archive of d35d92a5 for this record: with a planted record {"reality": "FOUNDER-USED (Linux container rehearsal, test key)", "run": "docker container"}, `python -m acceptance check` printed 'sound' and exited 0, and `python -m acceptance.claims` did not exist.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (constraint: 'Nothing built in a container is labelled founder-used, live or externally verified'; failure_evidence: 'a container run reported as founder-used')
INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (sections 10 inspection truth, 55 cathedral detector, 56 reality ladder, 67 kill criteria, 70 and 73)
baseline: 44b3df96 (unit base) and d35d92a5 (current #196 head): no greg/cathedral.py, no acceptance/claims.py, no 'cathedral' subcommand in greg/cli.py. The kill condition is parsed into UCLDocument.kill_conditions and never evaluated. The acceptance harness has one ordered LADDER (acceptance/__init__.py, shared with foundry.completion.EVIDENCE_TIERS) and TEST_TIERS ending at BODY_VERIFIED, but no reader holds evidence records to it. greg.metrics already separates the founder tier from test-key closures, and greg.path already separates the build frontier from achieved nodes.

alternatives.name: Proposed: a read-only cathedral detector and a reality-claim guard on the existing ladder, each pinned by a mutant gate
alternatives.description: greg/cathedral.py evaluates the kill condition's first clause over a window: activity from git objects on HEAD (commits, PR-like merges, new .md, .py and evidence READMEs) against founder-tier outcomes on the founder's designated body (closures as VEPMC's own row reads them, VEPMC founder_tier_count, achieved path nodes), with build-frontier progress reported beside them and never counted. Verdicts CATHEDRAL, NOT_CATHEDRAL or INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY; all thresholds in one THRESHOLDS table. `greg cathedral` prints the module's JSON. acceptance/claims.py (`python -m acceptance.claims`) reads 13 claim fields in JSON, JSON Lines and YAML under docs/, acceptance/ and every evidence directory, maps five vocabularies onto acceptance.LADDER through checked crosswalks, and fails a claim above the CEILINGS row of its declared or implied evidence kind. scripts/ci/check_cathedral_detector_mutants.py holds 160 mutants (107 on the guard, 53 on the detector).
advantages: The constitution's kill condition is computed for the first time, from git objects and the ledger, never from what markdown says
On d35d92a5 the planted inflated record passes every check; on this head `python -m acceptance.claims` fails it (1 violation, exit 1, ceiling BODY_VERIFIED)
No parallel ladder: one CEILINGS table on acceptance.LADDER, with five crosswalks tested total and monotone
Read-only: writes nothing, raises no founder ask, pauses and grants nothing
160/160 mutants caught on the merged head 1cc6645d, exit 0
disadvantages: In the build phase every real run is INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, so the detector cannot yet stop horizontal expansion by itself
The guard reads words, not meaning; known shapes still pass and are listed
A declared evidence_kind is the record's own word; the guard cannot verify that its reference proves the kind
Not wired into canonical-ci.yml; the mutant gate takes 24-39 minutes on this machine
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed. Revisit when a founder-designated body exists, when the integrator wires CI, or when a real founder-device record meets the guard.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: a written rule plus manual counts and a grep
alternatives.description: State the kill condition and the reality ladder in a README; count commits with `git log --since` and grep evidence JSON for FOUNDER-USED by hand when asked.
advantages: No new code and no new surface
disadvantages: A grep reads no negation, no ceiling and no evidence kind, so it flags honest records and misses inflated ones
Nothing fails; a sentence is a claim, not a check (directive section 56)
Commit counts alone ignore whether founder-tier outcomes moved, which is the other half of the condition
alternatives.revival_evidence: Only if the checks were already enforced elsewhere.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing: typed evidence records by schema, and activity from the GitHub API
alternatives.description: Require evidence_kind and evidence_ref on every evidence record through a JSON Schema and migrate the existing records; count PRs, reviews and agents from the GitHub API instead of merge shapes.
advantages: A typed field removes most lexical reading
Real PR counts instead of merge-shape inference
disadvantages: Migrating about 580 scanned files edits records that other open PRs own
The API needs network and a credential at every run; this checkout is a shallow clone and the container's network is policy-limited
The outcome side still needs the founder's ledger; a schema does not make a container run founder-used or not
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the founder or the integrator adopts an evidence-record schema for new records; the guard's evidence_kind and evidence_ref fields are already its seed.

alternatives.name: Staged: the claim guard now, the detector later
alternatives.description: Ship acceptance/claims.py alone and hold greg/cathedral.py until a founder-designated body exists, since every build-phase run is INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY.
advantages: No command whose only real verdict today is INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY
disadvantages: The kill condition stays unevaluated, and the conditional CATHEDRAL (activity rose, no founder-designated body) stays invisible
The detector's git safeguards (shallow, graft, partial clone, GIT_DIR) would wait for a body they do not depend on
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the integrator wants to take the guard and hold the detector; the two modules share no code and can be split by file.

pass_1.intended_outcome: The constitution's cathedral kill condition is computed from git and the founder's ledger, never from prose, and says plainly when history cannot decide. No machine-readable claim in the repository sits above what its evidence kind can establish, so no container or rehearsal run reads as founder-used, live or externally verified. No authority moves.

pass_2.attack_summary: Two review rounds by separate agents of this same session, each with an attack and a fidelity lens, attacked the guard's reading rules, the detector's git and ledger reads, the evidence README's numbers and the gap between the scope and what a real run produces. A verification then ran the mutant gate and found five unpinned safeguards, and a final verification re-ran everything on the head merged with d35d92a5. The work was interrupted by a spending stop on 2026-10-30 and resumed on 2026-11-04.

new_weaknesses.statement: Round 1: comma, dash, 'as required' and 'open' after a label hid the claim; any non-empty evidence_ref passed; lists, records, look-alike characters and key case were unread
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Only a status saying the label is unmet negates it, and not on a record describing a container, rehearsal or test run; ref_problem; NFKC normalisation, key-case and nested reading; 17 fixtures and mutants

new_weaknesses.statement: Round 1 and 2 on the detector: a graft cut history, a ledger that did not cover the window read as flat, a clock that ran ahead gave a false CATHEDRAL, GIT_DIR read another repository, a subdirectory or a partial clone read as complete, a U+001E path hid files, a merge's own files went uncounted
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Replace refs ignored and grafts refused; ledger and designation coverage checked; inversion refuses a cut where times run backwards; GIT_* dropped; --show-toplevel must equal the path; partial clones refused before any read; NUL-only parsing; -m with new-against-every-parent counting. Each has a test that failed before

new_weaknesses.statement: Round 2 on the guard: a negator reached across a comma or another label; 'above' and 'beyond' negated; MAC-VERIFIED, CHROMEBOOK-VERIFIED, suffixed labels and opening 'live' were unread; a unit test could claim INTEGRATION-TESTED; .jsonl, .JSON and acceptance YAML were unscanned; deep JSON crashed the guard
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: _reaches ends a negation at a comma, a conjunction or an unjoined label; NEGATORS narrowed; SOP and device crosswalks; section-56 ceiling per kind; extensions in any case and schemas by content; RecursionError and MemoryError make a file unreadable

new_weaknesses.statement: Five safeguards were behaviourally live but no test failed when they were removed (gate 155/160 at 954c6846)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Pinned in 631b40ec by fixtures x1-x6, a correct record, test_each_reading_rule_holds_on_its_own and a schema fixture; gate 160/160 on 631b40ec and on 1cc6645d

new_weaknesses.statement: The base moved three times during the unit (849c7973, fbce94e5, d35d92a5); the first two merges conflicted in greg/cli.py with the blockers and compute commands
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The cathedral dispatch moved beside its parser (ac78206b); both sides kept at each conflict; the third merge was clean; merge checks re-run at every head

new_weaknesses.statement: Four of the unit's commits carry the placeholder author 'combined-check <combined-check@local>' (3a0ebc73, dad4dc81, 780bacbf, 65f91d2f), and the round-2 fixes sat uncommitted across the 2026-10-30 spending stop

new_weaknesses.statement: The longer-label rule still reads 'not UNIT-TESTED FOUNDER-USED or LIVE-BOUNDED' as both LIVE and LIVE-BOUNDED

migration_plan: None required. Additive: two new read-only modules, one CLI subcommand, a mutant script, two test files and two lines in foundry/owned-source.json. No record, ledger or file format changes, and no existing record declares evidence_kind. The integrator chooses whether to add the mutant gate and `python -m acceptance.claims` as steps in canonical-ci.yml.

steps: Revert the commits on claude/cathedral-detector-20261030, or decline intake into #196
Neither tool writes anything, so no data needs restoring
To keep one tool, revert only the other module, its tests and its mutants

kill_criteria: `greg cathedral` or `python -m acceptance.claims` writes a file or ledger record, raises a founder ask, pauses or grants anything
The detector reports counts or a CATHEDRAL or NOT_CATHEDRAL verdict on a shallow clone, a grafted or partial clone, or a ledger that does not cover the window
A test-key, fixture, rehearsal, unappraised, refuted or off-body closure moves an outcome
The guard passes a container or rehearsal record labelled FOUNDER-USED, LIVE or EXTERNALLY-VERIFIED in a shape the README does not list
The guard defines a rung that is not on acceptance.LADDER
An honest record can only be passed by weakening a rule, not by rewording or an allowlist entry with reason and owner
The mutant gate counts a survivor, an import error or a syntax error as caught
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption, any merge, and what a conditional CATHEDRAL should do (the constitution names suspend_expansion_and_escalate(alfonso) as his response). The #196 integrator decides intake and the CI wiring. session_01Kucyfm6YBHMTjaiC1M9hqD owns the reversible draft. The five role positions are recorded by the implementing session; the adversarial reviews were done by separate agents of this same session, not by independent sessions or humans. All five roles recommend RETAIN; three dissents are recorded.
review_trigger: The first founder-signed first_founder_body designation (then run `greg cathedral --body` on a full clone); the integrator's CI-wiring decision; the first real founder-device record; any record found inflated through a listed shape; or the base moving again
